 Warm and humid Monday for Houston ahead a stormy Election Day
 Cold front headed to southeast Texas for election day
 Collin Myers , Meteorologist
 Rachel Briers , Meteorologist
 Published:  November 2, 2026 at 1:51 PM Tags:  forecast , Houston weather , Cold front , Fall , Election Day , November I Voted stickers are seen at an early voting polling place Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (AP Photo/George Walker IV) (George Walker Iv, Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved) Monday’s Forecast: 
 We started off warm and muggy Monday with some patchy fog. The warmth and high humidity will continue through the day with highs reaching into the mid 80s. A few isolated rain showers are possible but most of Southeast Texas will stay dry. 
 Election Day cold front: 
 We’re watching for some stormy weather on Election Day. Tuesday, a cold front will bring a threat of showers and some strong thunderstorms through the afternoon and early evening hours. 
 Election Day Front (Copyright 2025 by KPRC Click2Houston - All rights reserved.) Right now, it looks like the front should be moving through Houston in the mid afternoon with storms moving just ahead of the front. Storms should be out of Southeast Texas by 9-10 pm.
 Behind the front, we’ll see cooler and drier air filter in. This will move temperatures back to the 50s and 70s and drop the humidity to much more comfortable levels.
 Feeling more like fall this week Extended forecast: 
 The humidity is back in full force and will remain high through Monday. Election Day Tuesday’s front lowers morning temperatures back to the 50s, with afternoons in the 70s. A northwesterly wind will dry out the air, bringing a fantastic fall feel.
